title: String, StringBuffer and StringBuilder
context: What are the differences between String, StringBuffer and StringBuilder?

source.title: JavaGuide (Snailclimb): Java basics questions (2 of 3)
source.note: Translated and condensed into English; see content/sources/javaguide/NOTICE.md.

answer: `String` is immutable: any change creates a new object. `StringBuffer` and `StringBuilder` are mutable. `StringBuffer` synchronises its methods, so it is thread-safe but slower. `StringBuilder`, added in Java 5, has the same API without synchronisation and is the default for building strings in one thread. Use `String` for values that don't change and `StringBuilder` for loops and step-by-step building.

points.title: Immutable versus mutable
points.why: Each change to a String allocates a new object.

points.title: Thread safety
points.why: StringBuffer's methods are synchronised. StringBuilder is faster when a single thread owns it.
